# Getting Started

This page covers what you need before you can compile and run Monkey C code, and how to actually do it.

## Prerequisites

Before building anything, make sure you have the following installed.

**Rust** — the language Monkey C's compiler itself is written in. You need it to build the compiler from source.

**nasm** — a Netwide Assembler. This is what turns the assembly code generated by the compiler into machine code. Another assembler could work in its place, but nasm is what the project is built and tested against.

**gcc** — the GNU Compiler Collection. Here it isn't compiling your Monkey C code directly, it's used to link the object file produced by nasm into a final runnable binary. Another linker would also work, but gcc is the one assumed by the default setup.

**Monkey C code** — a source file written in Monkey C, using the `.MC` extension. This is the input the compiler expects. If you want to see what actual Monkey C code looks like before setting anything up, take a look at the [language guide](./language-guide.md).

## Setup Instructions

1. Clone the repository:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/Magicchess1244/monkey_c.git
   cd monkey_c
   ```

2. Compile the code:

   ```bash
   make run FILE=YourProgram.MC
   ```

   Replace `YourProgram.MC` with the path to the Monkey C source file you want to build and run. The `make run` target handles the full pipeline: compiling your source into assembly, assembling it with nasm, and linking it with gcc into a binary that gets run right after.

If any of these steps fail, check that all three prerequisites are on your `PATH` first — that's the most common cause of setup issues.
